overall: The AG found the Conservation Commission violated the Open Meeting Law because every "Other Business" topic on its December 6 notice lacked sufficient detail, and ordered future compliance; the abutter-notice claim failed.

allegations.summary: Complaint said the December 6 meeting notice topics, especially the Eagle Scout Project item, lacked enough detail for the public.
allegations.key_passage: Although the complaint focuses on the notice's insufficient detail with respect to the topic of Eagle Scout Project, we find that all the topics listed under "Other Business" lacked sufficient detail.

allegations.summary: Complaint asserted that abutters of the Dug Pond project should have received individual notice of the meeting and an opportunity to be heard.
allegations.key_passage: Except when meeting in executive session pursuant to G.L. c. 30A, § 21(a)(1), the Open Meeting Law does not require public bodies to provide additional notice of meetings to specific individuals or groups of individuals for topics discussed during a meeting.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
remedy_passage: We order the Commission's immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and we caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
